issues.description: The study reconstructs past events and then analyzes archival text messages, which is a retrospective design. Calling this a "prospective research design" is conceptually incorrect and risks overstating the study's ability to predict future attempts or establish temporality in the way a true prospective cohort would.
issues.quote: By reconstructing the timeline of recent suicidal behaviors through a retrospective clinical interview, we utilized a prospective research design to understand which features in text communications predicted suicide attempt

issues.description: The manuscript repeatedly frames findings as identifying risk "in real time," but all episode labels were assigned retrospectively after the fact. The analyses therefore demonstrate post hoc association with retrospectively defined periods, not real-time detection or prospective prediction.
issues.quote: To this end, we aimed to improve our ability to assess suicide risk dynamically in real time.

issues.description: The central exposure window is described inconsistently across the manuscript. This ambiguity affects the core design, comparability of episodes, and interpretation of all slope analyses.
issues.quote: two weeks preceding a suicide attempt as a means to capture the period of escalation towards a suicide attempt ... 1) past actual, interrupted, or aborted suicide attempts, using the one-week period prior to the attempt as a “suicide attempt episode” ... day of episode (numerical factor ranging from -14 to 0)

issues.description: The manuscript collapses actual attempts, interrupted attempts, aborted attempts, and even episodes with no enacted self-harm into a single "suicide attempt" category. These phenomena differ meaningfully in behavior, lethality, and clinical meaning, so combining them threatens validity of the main comparison.
issues.quote: (Note that reported ‘suicide attempts’ also included incidents in which no physical attempt was enacted but in which participants considered their planning or actions to constitute a higher level of suicidal intent than ‘suicide ideation’ so they subjectively endorsed making an attempt on the screener questions.)

issues.description: The depressed comparison condition mixes qualitatively different states (depressed mood and high stress). This makes the comparison category conceptually heterogeneous and harder to interpret, because language during stress may differ from language during depression for reasons unrelated to suicide risk.
issues.quote: 3) two-week episodes of depressed mood or high stress (not resulting in suicide ideation or attempt);

issues.description: The low-risk comparison condition is inconsistently described as both "positive mood" and "typical mood." A typical neutral mood episode is not equivalent to a positive mood episode, so this inconsistency obscures what the reference condition actually represents.
issues.quote: 4) two-week episode of typical mood (i.e., neither particularly positive nor negative mood and no ideation or attempt).

issues.description: Treating depressed episodes as "minimal/no risk" is conceptually problematic, especially in a sample of people with prior suicide attempts. Depression and high stress can carry substantial suicide risk, so the assigned risk hierarchy may be inaccurate and could distort interpretation of contrasts.
issues.quote: attempt episodes were considered “high risk,” ideation episodes were considered “moderate risk,” and depressed and positive episodes were considered “minimal/no risk.”

issues.description: Singular first-person pronoun use is treated as an indicator of rumination/self-focus, but this is an indirect and debated proxy. Pronoun frequency does not map cleanly onto rumination, so the operationalization may not validly capture the intended construct.
issues.quote: we tested whether use of first-person pronouns (as an indicator of rumination) was greater prior to suicide attempts

issues.description: Belongingness and perceived burdensomeness are inferred from simple counts or ratios of sent versus received texts. Those behavioral counts do not validly measure the interpersonal theory constructs, which concern subjective experiences and relationship quality, not mere messaging volume.
issues.quote: we tested whether suicide attempters demonstrated greater signs of disengagement from and burdensomeness on their social support networks prior to suicide attempts compared to other episodes by examining patterns in outgoing vs. incoming messages.

issues.description: Attempt episodes are anchored to a salient event (the attempt), but ideation/depressed/positive episodes are just selected two-week windows. Comparing slopes from day -14 to 0 assumes those windows are aligned to an equivalent endpoint, which is not established and undermines interpretation of differential trajectories.
issues.quote: 2) two-week episodes of suicide ideation (not resulting in a suicide attempt); 3) two-week episodes of depressed mood or high stress (not resulting in suicide ideation or attempt); and 4) two-week episode of typical mood ... A series of mixed-effects models were performed for each language feature with 3 fixed effects: episode type (4 levels: attempt, ideation, depressed, positive), day of episode (numerical factor ranging from -14 to 0)

issues.description: Only 46% of identified episodes had analyzable SMS data, and 6 of 33 recruited participants contributed no episode data. This large reduction substantially lowers the effective sample and raises concern that analyzed episodes differ systematically from non-analyzed ones.
issues.quote: Among the episodes queried during the lab interview, 134 (46%) episodes contained SMS data, collected from 27 different participants.

issues.description: Missing SMS data arose from encryption settings, inaccessible backups, and unavailable old devices. These are systematic causes of missingness and likely related to episode recency and technology use, so the data are unlikely to be missing at random.
issues.quote: a number of iPhone users had encryption settings on their phones that prevented third-party iPhone software from accessing text data... efforts to collection additional messages outside of their current mobile device were minimally successful.

issues.description: The manuscript presents mixed models as especially appropriate because of the amount of missing data. Mixed models can handle some incomplete repeated measures under restrictive assumptions, but they do not remedy systematic missingness from inaccessible devices/backups or missing-not-at-random patterns.
issues.quote: This approach also allowed us to maximize sources of variance by analyzing on the message level rather than only mean values by episode, and was especially appropriate for this dataset given the amount of ‘missing data’ (i.e., participants varied widely in terms of the number of episodes types they reported and for which they had text data).

issues.description: Despite the very large number of messages, the key high-risk condition is based on only 21 attempt episodes with SMS data. Statistical inference is therefore driven by a small number of higher-level units, which limits stability and precision of estimates.
issues.quote: Among the 21 attempts with corresponding SMS data

issues.description: The analysis leverages 189,478 messages, but the number of independent participants and episodes is small. Message-level modeling does not eliminate the fact that inference about suicide-risk states rests on relatively few people and episodes, so precision may be overstated if clustering is not fully modeled.
issues.quote: Across all episodes, 189,478 text messages were collected and analyzed ... This approach also allowed us to maximize sources of variance by analyzing on the message level rather than only mean values by episode

issues.description: For the key interaction analyses, the authors state that the appropriate random-effects structure included by-participant slopes, but then removed all random slopes when the model failed to converge. In a within-subject design, omitting necessary random slopes can inflate Type I error and undermine confirmatory inference.
issues.quote: The maximal random effects model appropriate for these data included random intercepts of participant, participant-episode, and message, and random by-participant slopes for episode type, day of episode, and episode type by day. Models with the full set of random slopes did not converge; therefore, no random slopes were included in the final model.

issues.description: Including a random intercept for each message is unusual because each message is the observation unit and appears only once. If this was intended as an observation-level random effect for overdispersion, that should be justified explicitly; otherwise the specification is unclear and potentially inappropriate.
issues.quote: A random by-participant slope for episode type and random intercepts of participant, participant-episode, and message were included as the random effects.

issues.description: The manuscript analyzes outcomes such as number of messages sent per day with linear mixed models on raw continuous values. Count outcomes are typically skewed and nonnegative, and ratios can be bounded and non-normal, so Gaussian LMMs may be misspecified without diagnostics or alternative count/beta models.
issues.quote: For outcome variables that were not proportion scores (e.g., number of messages sent per day), the raw continuous variable was used in a linear mixed-effects model (LMM), using the “lmer” function.

issues.description: The time predictor is described as a "numerical factor," which is internally ambiguous: a variable cannot simultaneously be treated as a continuous numeric slope and a categorical factor without materially different interpretations. The coding of time is essential for interpreting the interaction terms but is unclear.
issues.quote: day of episode (numerical factor ranging from -14 to 0)

issues.description: The manuscript states that the optimal window was assessed empirically via visual inspection of the data, which introduces researcher degrees of freedom. Selecting the analytic window after looking at the outcome trajectories can capitalize on noise, especially in a small pilot study.
issues.quote: The question of the optimal time window was also assessed empirically, using visual inspection of descriptive figures to identify when the rate of change appeared to be most pronounced... changes tended to occur most notably and often around 7 days prior to the suicide attempt.

issues.description: The study tests many outcomes and pairwise contrasts, and several highlighted findings are only marginally significant. Explicitly choosing not to adjust for multiplicity increases the likelihood that positive findings are false positives.
issues.quote: our analyses involved running a fairly large number of tests, which potentially increases the chances of rejecting the null hypothesis due to the sheer number of tests. Given this is a pilot study ... we decided not to artificially suppress Type I error (i.e., using a multiple comparisons correction)

issues.description: The manuscript reports additional analyses on alternate data subsets in a supplement, but does not clearly indicate whether these were pre-specified or how they affected inferential interpretation. Running the same outcomes across multiple subsets increases analytic flexibility and selective emphasis risk.
issues.quote: Additional analyses were performed to examine the same set of outcome variables but in different ways to examine the robustness of the primary results and to see if the pattern of results changed. Those analyses are available in Supplement 3 online.

issues.description: The power analysis is not aligned with the multilevel modeling actually used. Cramer's V and "chi-square tests of mixed-effects models" do not provide a transparent or appropriate basis for powering complex repeated-measures GLMMs with clustered observations, and the description of 30 attempters representing 60 attempts but only 20 with usable SMS data is internally confusing.
issues.quote: We determined that a sample size of 30 suicide attempters (representing 60 attempts but only 20 with collected, usable SMS data, divided by the design effect) would provide enough power to detect only large effect sizes (Cramer’s V=0.29) for chi-square tests of mixed-effects models comparing suicide attempts to other types of episodes

issues.description: The manuscript states that β values in log-odds units are standardized and serve as effect sizes. Logit coefficients are not inherently standardized, and using them as effect sizes without clear scaling or transformation is misleading.
issues.quote: Here, β (standardized values of the model parameter estimates in log odds units) are reported and serve as effect sizes.

issues.description: Likelihood-ratio tests and Wald chi-square tests are distinct inferential procedures. Describing them as a single test type is statistically incorrect and leaves readers unable to determine what test was actually used.
issues.quote: Likelihood-ratio (Wald chi-square) tests were performed to compare goodness of fit for models including and excluding the fixed effect of episode type.

issues.description: The reported means show desire to die increased from pre to post (0.82 to 1.03), yet the text says it "decreased slightly." This is a direct contradiction between the descriptive values and the narrative interpretation.
issues.quote: desire to die from pre (M=0.82, SD=1.10) to post (M=1.03, SD=0.90) significantly decreased slightly, t(32)=2.23, p=.033.

issues.description: The same omnibus test for sadness is reported with two different p-values. A chi-square of 8.74 with 3 df corresponds to p=.033, not p=.003, so at least one value is wrong.
issues.quote: Regarding sentiment, there was a significant effect of episode type on use of sad words, 2(3)=8.74, p=.003. / Sadness (sad) | 2=8.74 | 3 | 3 | .033

issues.description: The discussion states that attempt periods showed greater anxiety, but the results section explicitly states no significant effect for anxiety. This contradiction changes substantive interpretation of the findings.
issues.quote: No significant effects by episode type emerged for more general emotional content (i.e., positive emotion, negative emotion, emotional tone) or other specific emotions/constructs (i.e., anxiety, anger, death). / results indicated that the period of high risk just before a suicide attempt was associated with messages indicating greater anxiety and sadness.

issues.description: The primary models include only episode type and time, despite episodes differing in life context, calendar period, relationships, treatment status, and phone/platform history. Without controlling for such factors, observed language differences cannot be attributed uniquely to suicide risk state.
issues.quote: A series of mixed-effects models were performed with episode type as a within-subject fixed effect (4 levels: attempt, ideation, depressed, positive) and the language feature of interest as the outcome variable.

issues.description: The sample is predominantly young, female, White, and college-enrolled. Findings from this narrowly defined group should not be generalized broadly to older adults, men, more diverse populations, or clinical settings without caution.
issues.quote: Most of the participants were female, White, and college-aged.

issues.description: Participants with higher current suicidality were excluded. This restriction limits generalizability precisely to the individuals of greatest interest for imminent-risk detection.
issues.quote: Inclusion criteria included ... minimal or no current desire to die ... Any participants with intense thoughts of suicide who were determined to be at “high risk” or “imminent risk” for suicidal behavior ... were excluded from study participation

issues.description: The study necessarily sampled living participants with non-lethal or aborted/interrupted attempts. The authors acknowledge that suicide attempters can differ from suicide completers, so extrapolation to fatal suicidal behavior is limited.
issues.quote: logistics of accessing and downloading communication data necessitated enrolling participants with non-lethal attempts. It is possible that characteristics of suicide attempters differ from those of suicide completers

issues.description: Recruitment required both endorsement of a prior hopelessness period and access to historical digital communications. This likely selected a specific subgroup of attempters who are young, technologically connected, and willing to share archived messages, limiting representativeness.
issues.quote: On the participant pool pretest ... participants were asked, “Have you ever had a period of sadness in the past during which you felt hopeless?” ... Inclusion criteria included ... availability of and access to personal messaging data dating back prior to significant life events

issues.description: Participants with many lifetime events contributed only up to three episodes per type, but the manuscript does not explain how those episodes were chosen when more than three existed. This leaves room for selective inclusion based on recency, data availability, or salience.
issues.quote: For each episode type, we asked about a maximum of three episodes (e.g., three suicide attempts if participant has three or more lifetime attempts).

issues.description: The chosen text-analysis method cannot account for negation or context, meaning category scores can misclassify message meaning. This directly weakens inference that LIWC variables validly represent emotional or cognitive states in SMS data.
issues.quote: One weakness of this approach is that examining single words in isolation can fail to capture the semantic context of the word (e.g., “not happy” would count as “positive emotion” because negation is not accounted for)

issues.description: The paper concludes that it identified "novel predictors" that may predict acute risk, but no prospective validation, held-out prediction, sensitivity/specificity evaluation, or real-time deployment was performed in this study. Association within retrospectively labeled episodes does not establish predictive utility.
issues.quote: This laboratory investigation identified novel predictors of suicidal behaviors, which may be utilized in the future by machine learning models to predict acute suicide risk and identify whether and where an individual is on the pathway from thinking about suicide to acting on those thoughts.
